newsitem.title: USA: US late Gulf product diffs firm on refiner buying.
newsitem.headline: US late Gulf product diffs firm on refiner buying.

text.p: U.S. late spot products prices moved higher late Friday thanks to a firming in differentials on refiner buying, traders said, amid moderately lower February gasoline futures and stronger NYMEX heating oil.

USG conventional M4 gasoline for the front 4th cycle on the Colonial pipeline was talked between 1.25 cent and 1.00 cent below the February print, almost one cent firmer than Thursday diffs, players said.
"It was pretty spirited buying," one Gulf trader said, noting diffs had collapsed Thursday amid almost complete buyer disinterest.
Their newfound interest may have been spurred by news that Exxon took its 88,000 bpd catalytic cracker in Baytown, Texas into maintenance earlier this week.

In New York Harbor, most gasoline grades saw diffs snap back to Thursday levels after easing slightly Friday morning on news Tosco Corp had restarted its 140,000 barrel per day catalytic cracker at its refinery in Linden, New Jersey.
The unit had been taken down three weeks ago for maintenance in the aftermath of a fire in early December.
Gulf refinery buying also helped firm diffs on heating oil a half cent to about 3.75 cents below the print, traders said.
-- Ransdell Pierson, New York Energy Desk +1 212 859 1626
